Silhouette: Four-legged brown bear frame. Host frame: the brown bear sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature combining a european rhinoceros beetle and a brown bear. The head is that of the brown bear, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: brown bear body and legs, with its own dense fur on the face and a plain coat with no stripes or spots; from the european rhinoceros beetle, as parts and materials on the brown bear's own body: a head horn grown from the frontal bone above and between the eyes, emerging from the covering, which continues from there into the body covering of smooth, glossy dark cuticle, with one horn curving upward and back from the head, long and curved; hard, glossy chitin plates with fine seams in its own colors, grown from the skin as the brown bear's own covering over the crown of the head, neck, shoulders, back, flanks, belly, hips, legs and tail, replacing the brown bear's dense fur there and conforming to the brown bear's body as a few large, smooth, fused plates each spanning a whole body region of the brown bear (the shoulders, the back, the hips, each limb section), sized to the brown bear's body and joined by flexible cuticle at every joint; every covered part keeps the brown bear's own length and shape, and the tail stays the brown bear's own tail; the dense fur stops at the covering's edge, and the face keeps the brown bear's own dense fur. The covering follows the body's own shape and bends at every joint. Declared fiction: arthropod parts at large size, shown with thick supporting legs and rows of small breathing openings (spiracles) along the flanks. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (forest): dark back and light belly (mild countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Designing hybrid bear silhouette**
I'm planning the image around a brown bear outline with beetle-inspired details, placing a rhinoceros beetle horn above the eyes while keeping the head clear, eyes visible, and the coat plain without stripes or spots.
**Researching rhinoceros beetle anatomy**
I'm reviewing reference details for a European rhinoceros beetle to capture the horn shape, glossy chitin plates, and spiracles, so the illustration matches the described bear hybrid accurately.
**Composing hybrid bear illustration**
I'm building the T2I image with a brown bear head and body covered in chitin plates, a curved horn, spiracles along the flanks, and a side three-quarter view on a plain light background in a natural history style.
**Refining watercolor realism**
I'm planning a second generation with a more natural watercolor style and added photoreal detail so the spiracles and limbs look more realistic.
**Refining beetle integration**
I'm preparing another image using media_13iwlj as the base, removing the extra beetle and blending the remaining one more naturally into the watercolor scene.
